stem: Which associated description is most consistent with a congenital diaphragmatic hernia in a newborn with respiratory distress?

options.text: Usually right sided, without lung effects
Usually left sided with pulmonary hypoplasia
Usually central, with diffuse coarse densities

explanation: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia is usually left sided with pulmonary hypoplasia.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Page 196

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because congenital diaphragmatic hernia is usually left sided rather than right sided, and it is associated with lung hypoplasia.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because congenital diaphragmatic hernia is usually left sided and is associated with pulmonary hypoplasia.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because diffuse coarse densities are more in keeping with meconium aspiration than congenital diaphragmatic hernia.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because resolution by 48 hours is typical of transient tachypnoea of the newborn, not diaphragmatic hernia.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because congenital diaphragmatic hernia presents at birth or in the neonatal period, not only beyond infancy.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
